speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify the nature of your double vision—does it worsen when you look up or down, and is there any drooping of your eyelids? Additionally, have you experienced difficulty swallowing or speaking recently?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of weakness worsening with activity and improving with rest is very suggestive of a neuromuscular junction disorder. Have you noticed any muscle twitching or a sensation of heaviness in your eyelids or face? Also, do you smoke, and if so, for how long?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_receptor_antibodies, Repeated_Nerve_Conduction_Study.
